Short Description (about 500 words):
MEGWARE Computer Vertrieb und Service GmbH is one of Europe’s leading providers of high-performance computing (HPC) and AI-ready infrastructure solutions. The company delivers advanced, custom-built systems that enable industrial clients, universities, and research institutions to run HPC and AI applications efficiently, covering the full value chain—from consulting and system design to development, sales, implementation, and long-term service. To date, MEGWARE has successfully delivered more than 1,300 HPC and AI infrastructure projects across Europe and beyond.

Founded in 1990 and headquartered in Chemnitz, Germany, MEGWARE initially established itself as a provider of comprehensive IT solutions. Over nearly three decades, the company has distinguished itself through technological ingenuity, customer proximity, and exceptional flexibility. In 2000, MEGWARE entered the field of high-performance computing with its first major HPC project. The MEGWARE “CLiC” system, developed for Chemnitz University of Technology, achieved the best price-performance ratio worldwide and reached position 126 on the prestigious TOP500 list of the world’s fastest supercomputers.

HPC at MEGWARE

High-performance computing remains MEGWARE’s core business. A dedicated team of HPC engineers develops production-ready systems and software platforms that combine high performance, energy efficiency, and operational reliability. A key in-house hardware development is EUREKA®, a modular, high-density HPC compute platform with fully fanless direct liquid cooling. Designed for extreme power densities and ASHRAE W45 compliance, EUREKA® enables energy-efficient operation, supports heat reuse concepts, and ensures high availability through hot-pluggable components and detailed power and energy monitoring.

AI at MEGWARE

Artificial Intelligence is a rapidly growing focus area within MEGWARE’s technology portfolio, building on its HPC expertise. The company designs and delivers AI-ready infrastructures optimized for machine learning, deep learning, and data-intensive workloads, combining high-performance compute nodes, GPU acceleration, high-speed interconnects, and scalable storage architectures. Leveraging its in-house hardware platforms and software solutions, MEGWARE enables customers to deploy, operate, and scale AI workloads efficiently while maintaining full control over performance, reliability, and total cost of ownership.

Short Description (about 500 words):
Mistral AI is a leading European AI research laboratory based in Paris, focused on developing state-of-the-art open large language models. Founded by former researchers from Meta and DeepMind, Mistral has quickly become a cornerstone of the European AI ecosystem. Their models, such as Mistral 7B and Mixtral 8x7B, are known for their efficiency and high performance, often outperforming much larger closed models.

Mistral AI emphasizes transparency and openness, providing weights for many of their models to enable researchers and developers to build on their work without being locked into proprietary APIs. The company aims to provide a reliable European alternative in the AI space, focusing on data privacy and sovereignty. Their business model includes commercial offerings such as Mistral La Plateforme, providing managed access to their flagship models.

With significant funding and a team of world-class AI engineers, Mistral AI is pushing the boundaries of what is possible with generative AI, ensuring that Europe remains a global leader in artificial intelligence innovation. Their approach to efficient model scaling and sparse architectures has set new standards in the industry, making advanced AI accessible to a wider range of hardware and applications.

DeepL is a German AI company headquartered in Cologne, renowned for producing the world's most accurate machine translation service. Utilizing advanced neural network architectures, DeepL Translate consistently outperforms competitors by capturing subtle nuances and context that other services often miss. The company's focus on quality and linguistic precision has made it the preferred choice for professional translators and international corporations alike.

Beyond its flagship translation web service, DeepL offers a powerful API for integrating translation into business workflows and a specialized tool for AI-enhanced writing, DeepL Write. DeepL's success is rooted in its proprietary data processing techniques and custom supercomputing hardware, which allow for rapid training and deployment of large-scale language models.

As a global leader in communication AI, DeepL continues to expand its language support and feature set, aiming to break down language barriers across the globe while maintaining a strict commitment to data security and European privacy standards.

Short Description (about 500 words):
SiPearl is a French-based semiconductor company dedicated to designing Rhea, the world's first high-performance, low-power microprocessor for supercomputers. As a key player in the European Processor Initiative (EPI), SiPearl's mission is to secure Europe's technological sovereignty in the high-stakes field of high-performance computing.

The Rhea processor is based on ARM Neoverse technology and is specifically optimized for exascale supercomputing, offering high memory bandwidth and energy efficiency. SiPearl works closely with European partners like Atos and research centers to ensure Rhea meets the demanding requirements of future HPC workloads, from climate modeling to medical research.

By developing its own chip, Europe aims to reduce its dependency on non-European technology for its most critical infrastructure. SiPearl's design philosophy focuses on power efficiency and high performance per watt, addressing the major energy challenges of next-generation supercomputing. The company's roadmap includes future generations of processors that will further integrate European IP and RISC-V components, solidifying Europe's position as a leader in chip design for HPC and AI.

Short Description (about 500 words):
Aleph Alpha is a German AI research and application company focused on the development of large-scale generative AI models for B2B and public sector applications. Based in Heidelberg, the company is known for its Luminous model family, which offers state-of-the-art performance in multiple European languages.

A key differentiator for Aleph Alpha is its commitment to data sovereignty, transparency, and traceability, making its solutions particularly attractive for highly regulated industries and government entities. Their technology is designed to be explainable, allowing users to understand the reasoning behind AI-generated outputs, which is critical for trust and compliance.

Aleph Alpha operates its own high-performance compute infrastructure to train its models, ensuring full control over the AI lifecycle. By focusing on industrial and complex administrative use cases, Aleph Alpha is positioning itself as Europe's leading provider for critical AI applications that require more than just creative text generation—they require reliability, security, and a deep understanding of European values and regulatory frameworks.

Eviden, part of the Atos Group, is a global leader in data-driven, trusted, and sustainable digital transformation. As Europe's premier supercomputing manufacturer, Eviden produces the BullSequana range of supercomputers, which power some of the world's most advanced research centers.

Eviden's expertise spans the entire spectrum of high-performance computing, from hardware design and integration to software development and cybersecurity. The company is also at the forefront of quantum computing research, offering a quantum computing simulation platform to prepare researchers for the post-NISQ era.

Eviden integrates AI capabilities into its HPC solutions, enabling hybrid workloads that combine traditional simulation with machine learning. With a strong presence in defense and national security, Eviden's solutions are built with a focus on sovereignty and high-level protection. The company's commitment to sustainability is reflected in its liquid cooling technologies and energy-efficient systems, aiming to minimize the environmental impact of large-scale computing. Eviden serves a diverse range of clients, from academic institutions to Fortune 500 companies, providing the compute power necessary to solve the world's most complex challenges.

Subdomains: Neutral Atom Quantum Computing; Quantum Simulation;
Technologies: Neutral Atoms; Laser Trapping; Quantum Softwares;
Short Description (about 500 words):
Pasqal is a French quantum computing company that builds quantum processors from neutral atoms. Founded by Nobel Prize winner Alain Aspect and other leading physicists, Pasqal is developing a scalable and powerful quantum platform capable of solving problems that are currently beyond the reach of classical supercomputers.

Their technology uses lasers to trap and manipulate individual atoms, turning them into programmable qubits. This approach offers significant advantages in scaling to hundreds and eventually thousands of qubits while maintaining high coherence.

Pasqal is not only a hardware provider but also develops a full software stack, including the Pulser environment, to enable users to program their quantum processors for specific use cases in optimization, materials science, and drug discovery. The company has already established partnerships with major industrial players like Eni and BMW, demonstrating the practical application of their quantum technology. Pasqal is a key contributor to the European quantum ecosystem, aiming to provide exascale-class quantum advantage within this decade.

Graphcore is a semiconductor company that has developed a new type of processor, the Intelligence Processing Unit (IPU), specifically designed for artificial intelligence. While headquartered in the UK, Graphcore has significant operations and a strong European focus, recently becoming a part of the SoftBank family with continued R&D in Norway and across the EU.

The IPU architecture is uniquely suited to the sparse and high-dimensional computations required by modern machine learning models, offering significant performance gains over traditional GPUs. Graphcore's Poplar software stack makes it easy for developers to adapt their existing models from frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch to the IPU.

Their systems, ranging from individual accelerator cards to the Bow Pod supercomputers, are being used by research institutes and companies to accelerate breakthroughs in everything from climate modeling to medical imaging. Graphcore's focus on innovative chip architecture reflects the global shift towards specialized AI hardware, with the company aiming to provide the most efficient platform for the next generation of AI research.

Legal Entity Name: European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
Short Description (about 500 words):
The European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) is a legal and funding entity created in 2018 to enable the European Union and EuroHPC participating countries to coordinate their efforts and pool their resources with the objective of making Europe a world leader in supercomputing.

This includes developing a world-class supercomputing ecosystem, acquiring and deploying in the EU a world-class supercomputing and data infrastructure, and supporting the development of innovative supercomputing technologies and applications. EuroHPC JU has co-funded the acquisition of several of the world's fastest supercomputers, such as LUMI in Finland, Leonardo in Italy, and MareNostrum 5 in Spain, and is currently preparing for the first European exascale system, JUPITER.

These systems are available to European researchers and industrial users, including SMEs, to run large-scale simulations and AI workloads. Through its research and innovation agenda, EuroHPC JU also supports the development of European hardware and software components, fostering a sovereign and competitive European HPC supply chain.

IQM is the European leader in building quantum computers. Based in Espoo, Finland, the company builds quantum processors for supercomputing centers and industrial customers using superconducting qubit technology.

IQM is unique in its approach of developing application-specific quantum processors, co-designing hardware and software to solve specific problems more efficiently. They have delivered the first Finnish commercial quantum computer and are a key partner in several European quantum initiatives, including the development of Germany's first world-class quantum computer.

IQM's full-stack approach encompasses everything from chip design and fabrication in their own cleanroom facility to the development of the software stack and user interface. The company aims to achieve quantum advantage through a combination of high-fidelity qubits and optimized architectures, positioning Europe as a key player in the global quantum race. With offices across Europe, IQM is building a pan-European quantum ecosystem, collaborating with research institutes and industrial partners to bring quantum computing to practical use.

MainConcept is a leading provider of high-quality video and audio codecs and processing components. In the realm of HPC, MainConcept offers specialized software development kits (SDKs) that are highly optimized for multi-core processors and specialized instruction sets like Intel AVX-512.

Their technology is used by high-performance broadcasting and streaming platforms to deliver ultra-high-definition content at scale. By leveraging HPC infrastructure, MainConcept's encoders can process massive amounts of video data in real-time or with significantly reduced turnaround times.

The company's focus on efficiency and performance makes it a key partner for media companies looking to optimize their processing workflows while maintaining the highest visual quality. With decades of experience in codec development, MainConcept continues to innovate with the latest standards like VVC and AV1, ensuring that European video technology remains at the cutting edge of global media distribution.

ParTec is a German HPC company specializing in the design, construction, and management of complex supercomputer systems. They are pioneers of the Modular Supercomputing Architecture (MSA), which allows different types of compute modules (like CPUs, GPUs, and quantum processors) to be seamlessly integrated into a single system.

ParTec's flagship software product, ParaStation MPI, is a high-performance communication layer that provides the scalability and low latency required for exascale computing. The company is a key partner in the EuroHPC JUPITER project, Europe's first exascale supercomputer.

ParTec provides not only software but also extensive engineering services, from system design to operational support, ensuring that large-scale systems are optimized for scientific research. Their focus on modularity and open standards makes them a central player in the development of a sovereign European HPC infrastructure, capable of integrating a wide variety of emerging technologies.

Quobly (formerly Siquance) is a French quantum computing startup that leverages the enormous power of the semiconductor industry to build quantum processors. Based in Grenoble, Quobly uses silicon spin qubit technology, which is compatible with standard CMOS manufacturing processes.

This approach offers a clear path to mass-producing qubits, potentially scaling to millions of qubits much more easily than other technologies. Quobly's mission is to build a high-performance quantum computer that can be manufactured using existing European semiconductor foundries.

By bridging the gap between quantum physics and industrial-scale manufacturing, Quobly aims to provide the hardware foundation for the next generation of computing. The company is a spin-off from CEA and CNRS, benefiting from decades of research in silicon electronics and quantum physics. Their focus on the "quantum dot" approach positions them uniquely in the European ecosystem as a hardware provider with a highly scalable roadmap.

Gcore is an international provider of edge and cloud solutions, headquartered in Luxembourg. They offer a powerful AI Cloud platform that provides access to world-class hardware like NVIDIA GPUs and Graphcore IPUs, enabling companies of all sizes to train and deploy complex AI models.

Gcore's global network infrastructure, including a high-performance CDN and edge computing nodes, allows AI applications to be delivered with low latency to users worldwide. The company provides a full suite of managed services, from managed Kubernetes to AI-as-a-service, simplifying the deployment of AI-ready infrastructure.

Gcore's focus on building a sustainable and efficient cloud is reflected in their choice of data centers and hardware. By providing easy access to cutting-edge AI accelerators, Gcore is a vital enabler for the European AI startup ecosystem, providing the compute power needed to compete on a global scale.

Terraform Industries (European division) specializes in using high-performance computing and AI to create accurate digital twins of the Earth's climate. Their platform enables researchers and policymakers to simulate various climate scenarios with unprecedented detail, helping to predict the impact of environmental changes and evaluate the effectiveness of mitigation strategies.

By combining traditional physical models with advanced machine learning techniques, Terraform Industries can deliver faster and more accurate simulations than previously possible. Their work is critical for industries like insurance and agriculture, which are highly sensitive to climate risks.

Based in the Netherlands, the company leverages the country's strong tradition in water management and climate research, collaborating with European supercomputing centers to run their massive workloads. Terraform's mission is to provide the data and insights necessary to build a more resilient and sustainable future, using the most advanced computing tools available.

Alice & Bob is a French startup developing a universal error-corrected quantum computer. Their unique approach uses "cat qubits," a type of superconducting qubit that has built-in resistance to bit-flip errors.

This architectural choice significantly reduces the overhead required for quantum error correction, which is the biggest hurdle to building a useful quantum computer. Alice & Bob's mission is to reach fault-tolerant quantum computing much faster than with traditional qubit designs.

The company is building a full quantum stack and offers access to their initial processors through a cloud platform. By focusing on reliability and scalability from the start, Alice & Bob aims to provide the compute power needed for applications like molecular simulation and complex optimization. Based in Paris, the company is a leading light in the French quantum ecosystem, attracting top talent and significant investment to build a sovereign European quantum advantage.

Scaleway is a French cloud service provider that offers a wide range of infrastructure solutions, with a strong current focus on AI and high-performance computing. Scaleway emphasizes European data sovereignty and privacy, making it a preferred choice for companies concerned about where their data is processed. Their ecosystem includes managed Kubernetes, serverless functions, and high-performance storage, providing a complete platform for building and scaling AI applications.

Scaleway is also committed to environmental sustainability, operating some of the most energy-efficient data centers in France. By combining cutting-edge technology with a commitment to European values, Scaleway is a key infrastructure provider for the continent's digital economy.

Eurotech is an Italian multinational that specializes in the design and development of edge computers, industrial PCs, and high-performance embedded systems. In the context of HPC, Eurotech is known for its legendary Aurora supercomputers, which pioneered the use of hot water liquid cooling.

Today, the company focuses on bringing HPC capabilities to the edge—the "Edge HPC." Their systems are designed for extreme environments, providing high-density compute power for real-time AI applications in transportation, defense, and energy sectors.

Eurotech provides a full software stack (Everyware Software Framework) to manage and secure these edge devices at scale. Their expertise in liquid cooling and miniaturized HPC architecture allows them to deliver significant compute power in small, energy-efficient forms. Eurotech is a key contributor to European research projects and continues to push the boundaries of where supercomputing can be applied.

Orange Business, the enterprise division of the Orange Group, provides a comprehensive set of AI and data services to help organizations navigate their digital transformation.

Their offerings include AI strategy consulting, data management, and the implementation of machine learning operations (MLOps) platforms. Orange Business leverages its extensive network and cloud infrastructure to deliver secure and scalable AI solutions.

They have a strong focus on sovereign and trusted cloud environments, particularly important for European clients in sensitive sectors. By combining connectivity, cybersecurity, and data expertise, Orange Business enables companies to integrate AI into their business processes effectively. Their global reach and local presence in many European countries make them a major partner for large-scale AI deployments across the continent.

Atos, through its Bull brand, is Europe's leading manufacturer of supercomputers and a global player in the HPC market. Their BullSequana XH range is designed for the largest-scale simulations and AI workloads, powering many of the top supercomputing centers in the world.

Atos is at the forefront of the exascale race, developing systems with advanced liquid cooling and low-carbon footprints. Their expertise includes the entire HPC stack, from specialized interconnects and server blades to orchestration and energy management software.

Atos is also a key player in the European Processor Initiative, aiming to integrate European-designed chips into their systems. Beyond hardware, Atos provides extensive consulting and support services, helping scientific and industrial users optimize their applications for highly parallel architectures. As a cornerstone of the European tech landscape, Atos is vital for the continent's strategic autonomy in high-end computing.

Short Description (about 500 words):
SambaNova Systems, while US-headquartered, has a strong and growing presence in Europe, with key installations and development teams in Germany and across the EU. They offer a comprehensive AI platform built around their unique Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit (RDU), which is designed to accelerate both training and inference for large language models and complex AI workloads.

SambaNova's "AI is a Service" model provides enterprises with pre-trained models and the hardware to run them, simplifying the adoption of generative AI. Their systems are known for their high memory capacity and performance, particularly for long-context models.

In Europe, SambaNova works with leading research centers, such as the Juelich Supercomputing Centre, to explore the integration of their dataflow architecture into large-scale HPC environments. Their focus on the full stack—from chips to models—positions them as a unique player in the European AI infrastructure market.

Quantum Computing Inc. (QCI) operates a European division focused on delivering accessible and practical quantum solutions. Their technology is based on photonic quantum computing and entropy quantum computing, which can run at room temperature and solve complex optimization problems.

QCI's flagship Dirac system is designed to handle high-dimensional calculations that are challenging for classical systems. In Europe, QCI focuses on industrial applications in logistics, supply chain management, and cybersecurity.

They provide a software platform that allows users to submit problems to their quantum hardware without needing deep expertise in quantum mechanics. By offering room-temperature, rack-ready systems, QCI is pushing the boundaries of where quantum technologies can be deployed, moving from specialized labs to standard data center environments.

Short Description (about 500 words):
Aon is a leading global professional services firm that has expanded its expertise into the realm of AI risk management and insurance. With a strong presence across Europe, Aon helps companies navigate the complexities of deploying AI, focusing on model reliability, bias detection, and regulatory compliance.

They offer specialized insurance products to protect against AI-related failures and liabilities. Aon's AI risk assessment tools use advanced analytics to evaluate the performance and safety of AI systems, providing organizations with the confidence to scale their AI initiatives.

Their consulting teams work with clients to build robust AI governance frameworks, ensuring alignment with European regulations like the AI Act. As AI becomes integral to business operations, Aon's role in mitigating associated risks is becoming increasingly critical for the European corporate sector.

Baidu, the leading Chinese AI company, maintains a significant research presence in Europe through its German and pan-European labs. Their EU-based researchers focus on fundamental AI topics such as natural language processing, computer vision, and autonomous driving.

Baidu's open-source deep learning platform, PaddlePaddle, is increasingly used by European developers for building AI applications. The company also collaborates with European automotive companies on autonomous driving technology through its Apollo platform.

Baidu's European operations bridge the gap between Asian and European AI ecosystems, fostering international collaboration in high-end research. Their work in large-scale language models (ERNIE) and its application in different linguistic contexts is a key focus for their European teams, contributing to the global progress of AI technology.

Cognite is a Norwegian leader in industrial AI software, providing the Cognite Data Fusion (CDF) platform to help heavy industries unlock the value of their data. CDF collects and contextualizes massive amounts of data from industrial operations—from sensors to 3D models—creating a comprehensive digital twin.

This data-ready foundation allows companies to build and scale AI applications for predictive maintenance, production optimization, and safety improvement. Cognite's technology is used by major global companies like Aker BP and Saudi Aramco to drive efficiency and sustainability in their operations.

The company is a key player in the European industrial tech scene, pushing the boundaries of how AI can be applied in complex, real-world environments. With a strong focus on data engineering and user-friendly interfaces, Cognite is making industrial data accessible and actionable for engineers and data scientists alike.

Terra is a Spanish AI company specializing in the analysis of geo-spatial and satellite data to monitor environmental changes and improve agricultural productivity. Their platform uses advanced deep learning algorithms to process high-resolution satellite imagery, identifying patterns and anomalies that are crucial for climate action and resource management.

Terra's solutions are used by governments and international organizations to track deforestation, monitor water levels, and optimize crop yields. Based in Madrid, the company leverages Spain's strong expertise in environmental science and remote sensing, collaborating with European space agencies and research centers.

Terra's mission is to provide the data-driven insights needed for sustainable land management and climate resilience, using AI to turn raw environmental data into actionable knowledge.

EnSilica is a leading designer of custom ASICs (Application Specific Integrated Circuits) for high-performance computing, AI, and communications applications. With design centers in the UK and across Europe, EnSilica provides full turnkey design services, from specification to supply of finished chips.

Their expertise include high-speed networking, AI acceleration, and low-power hardware design. EnSilica's own IP, such as the eSi-RISC processor family, is used to build efficient and specialized chips for a variety of markets, including automotive and industrial automation.

As the demand for specialized AI hardware grows, EnSilica helps European companies develop their own sovereign silicon, optimized for their specific requirements. Their deep understanding of semiconductor manufacturing and advanced packaging makes them a vital partner in the European chip ecosystem.

Seldon is a leader in the MLOps space, providing tools to simplify and scale the deployment, monitoring, and management of machine learning models. Their open-source platform, Seldon Core, is used by thousands of organizations worldwide to turn ML models into production-ready microservices.

Seldon's enterprise offerings add advanced features for model monitoring, drift detection, and explainability (Alibi), ensuring that AI systems are reliable, fair, and compliant. Based in the UK with a strong European user base, Seldon is at the forefront of the movement towards more robust and professional AI engineering.

Their focus on cloud-native architectures and open standards makes their solutions highly flexible and integrable. Seldon's mission is to help companies bridge the gap between data science and production, accelerating the time-to-value for machine learning projects.

Quantinuum, formed by the merger of Honeywell Quantum Solutions and Cambridge Quantum, is the world's largest integrated quantum computing company. While global in reach, its European operations in the UK and across the EU are central to its hardware research and software development.

Quantinuum builds high-fidelity trapped-ion quantum processors (H-Series) and develops a comprehensive software stack, including the TKET compiler and the InQuanto platform for quantum chemistry. Their technology is used by leading pharmaceutical and chemical companies to accelerate drug discovery and materials development.

Quantinuum is also a pioneer in quantum-natural language processing and quantum-enhanced cybersecurity. Their commitment to building a full-stack, hardware-agnostic ecosystem makes them a key driver of the global quantum industry, with a strong emphasis on scientific excellence and practical applications.

Nebulon provides "smart infrastructure" for high-performance and AI workloads, combining cloud-managed storage with on-premises hardware. Their Services Processing Unit (SPU) is a PCIe card that offloads storage and management tasks from the server CPU, providing consistent performance and simplified operations.

Nebulon's cloud-based control plane allows for automated deployment and management of massive infrastructure, ideal for scaling AI clusters. In Europe, Nebulon focuses on providing efficient and secure storage solutions for edge computing and private clouds.

Their technology enables organizations to build sovereign and high-performing data environments with the ease of use of a public cloud. By reducing the overhead of infrastructure management, Nebulon helps IT teams focus on delivering value from their data and AI applications.

Aethra Computing is a German startup focused on making high-performance computing more accessible and easier to manage in cloud-native environments. They provide a platform that integrates traditional HPC schedulers like Slurm with modern orchestration tools like Kubernetes, enabling users to run hybrid workloads efficiently.

Aethra's technology simplifies the provisioning of GPU clusters and the management of complex AI and simulation jobs. Their mission is to bridge the gap between the scientific computing world and the modern DevOps ecosystem.

Based in Munich, the company works with research institutes and industrial R&D teams to optimize their compute resources and accelerate their innovation cycles. Aethra's focus on open-source and standard technologies makes their solution highly adaptable and future-proof.

T-Systems, the business customer division of Deutsche Telekom, provides a comprehensive set of managed HPC and AI services. They offer access to high-performance compute resources through the Open Telekom Cloud, with a strong focus on data sovereignty and security, meeting the strict requirements of European organizations.

T-Systems' HPC experts help clients design, migrate, and operate their large-scale computing workloads, from automotive crash simulations to medical research. The company also provides specialized AI platforms for model training and deployment, integrating the latest hardware and software from partners like NVIDIA.

T-Systems' role as a trusted European cloud provider makes it a key partner for public sector entities and industries that require the highest levels of data protection and operational reliability.

Riverlane is building the operating system for quantum computers, Deltaflow.OS. Their mission is to solve the biggest challenge in quantum computing: error correction. By providing a high-performance software and hardware layer that interfaces directly with the quantum hardware, Riverlane enables qubits to perform more complex calculations with fewer errors.

Their technology is hardware-agnostic, working with various types of qubits, from superconducting to trapped ions. Based in Cambridge, Riverlane collaborates with leading quantum hardware companies and research groups worldwide.

Their work is essential for making quantum computers useful for practical applications in chemistry, materials science, and cryptography. Riverlane's team of physicists, engineers, and computer scientists are at the forefront of the global effort to build a fault-tolerant quantum computer.

Nabla is a French AI company dedicated to transforming healthcare with a digital medical assistant. Their platform uses advanced natural language processing to help doctors automate administrative tasks, such as clinical documentation and patient communication, allowing them to focus more on patient care.

Nabla's AI is built with a strong focus on privacy and data security, complying with medical regulations and ensuring that patient data is handled ethically. Based in Paris, the company is part of the vibrant French AI ecosystem, leveraging the country's strong talent pool in machine learning and medicine.

Nabla's mission is to make healthcare more efficient and accessible through the power of artificial intelligence, providing doctors with the tools they need to deliver better outcomes.

Oxford Quantum Circuits (OQC) is a leading European quantum computing company that builds quantum processors using a unique three-dimensional architecture called the "Coaxmon." This design offers superior scalability and performance by reducing the complexity of the wiring needed to control the qubits.

OQC provides access to its quantum computers through a cloud platform (OQC Toshiko) and through partnerships with major cloud providers. Their mission is to make quantum computing accessible to enterprise customers, enabling them to solve problems that are currently impossible.

Based in Oxford, the company is a key player in the UK's thriving quantum ecosystem, attracting top international talent and collaborating with global partners to drive the adoption of quantum technology.

LightOn is a French AI company that pioneered the use of optical computing for accelerating large-scale machine learning. Their Optical Processing Unit (OPU) uses light to perform massive matrix-vector multiplications, offering extreme energy efficiency and speed for specific AI tasks.

Today, LightOn also focuses on the software layer with its Paradigm platform, which helps organizations deploy and manage large language models (LLMs) securely. LightOn is a key contributor to the development of the first European LLMs, emphasizing data sovereignty and efficiency.

Based in Paris, the company bridges the worlds of high-tech hardware and advanced AI software, providing the tools needed for sustainable and powerful artificial intelligence. Their mission is to provide an alternative, more efficient path for the next generation of AI compute.

Short Description (about 500 words):
Helsing is a European defense tech company that builds AI-powered software to protect democracies. Their platform processes data from multiple sensors in real-time to provide high-level situational awareness and decision support for defense and security organizations.

Helsing's technology is designed to run at the edge, on various platforms from aircraft to ground vehicles, ensuring performance in communication-denied environments. Based in Berlin, with offices in London and Paris, Helsing is a pan-European effort to ensure that the continent remains technologically competitive in the defense sector.

The company emphasizes ethical AI and human-in-the-loop systems, adhering to the values of democratic societies. Helsing's mission is to provide the software foundation for a sovereign and technologically advanced European defense.

Pasqal's Quantum Cloud provides direct access to its neutral atom quantum processors for users worldwide. Through a simple web API and the open-source Pulser SDK, researchers and developers can program and run quantum simulations and optimizations on real quantum hardware.

This service is a key part of Pasqal's strategy to democratize quantum computing, enabling a wider range of users to explore the potential of the technology. The cloud platform provides a comprehensive environment for developing and testing quantum algorithms, with support for various application domains.

By offering easy access to its world-class quantum hardware, Pasqal is helping to build a global community of quantum developers and accelerate the path to practical quantum advantage. The service is hosted on secure European infrastructure, ensuring data privacy and sovereignty.

BioMed X is an independent research institute based in Heidelberg that uses high-performance computing and AI to accelerate breakthroughs in medicine and biotechnology. They operate at the intersection of academia and industry, bringing together top talent from around the world to solve complex biomedical challenges.
